newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn calls Sierra Leone coup a blow for democracy.
newsitem.headline: Bonn calls Sierra Leone coup a blow for democracy.

text.p: Germany on Monday condemned the weekend military coup in Sierra Leone, calling it a serious blow for democracy in West Africa, and appealed to the coup leaders to refrain from any further violence.
"The Federal government condemns this fresh, violent take-over of power by the military in Sierra Leone in the sharpest way," the German Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
The ministry called for the restoration of constitutional order and said the safety of civilians, members of the deposed government and foreigners in the country had to be guaranteed.

It said the German government was "deeply concerned" about attacks on United Nations facilities in the country, the arrest of UN personnel and the plundering of aid supplies and warned Germans about travelling there.
It said the government would closely follow further developments in the country and observe the behaviour of the new holders of power in respect to human rights and democracy.
Army major Johnny Paul Koromah declared himself head of state in Sierra Leone on Monday after seizing power and ousting the government elected only a year ago.
